p4a4: If you push past a reaction, the part of you behind it can learn that you still don't listen when it says no. You could tell it something like, "I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you. What's going on?" Or however you'd actually say that. Then wait. Don't grill the silence, and if nothing comes, don't answer for that part just because you'd set this up as a healing session.
p3c3: If it's an old part looking out for you, and you actually hear it when it warns you, it doesn't need to raise its voice. Your little one is picking up on how all your parts treat each other, which I think matters a lot more than what you end up calling them. When the inherited critic voice goes "oh, here we go again," or nobody answers at all, the part that warned you learns it has to shout.
p5c2: Sometimes a voice, hunch or presence does answer, and you can listen without letting it take over. Follow its advice if it's loving, wise and helpful and leaves you free, but recheck anything big or hard to undo, once you're calm, against what's really happened (if you're in danger, get safe first). Those checks are only for advice, though. If what comes is a hard feeling, you'd hear it out whether it passes them or not. When nothing answers, watch what sets the reaction off, what it does in your body, and what it makes you do or avoid. You can guess what the reaction is protecting you from, but it might actually prevent something else.
